figures.caption: Figure 4: Planning success rate: (Top) Closed-loop planning successcomparing 3DPWM (with and without the completion module), Partial 3DPWM, and ParticleFormer+. 3DPWM achieves the highest success across all tasks. (Bottom) Open-loop planning success on the same tasks, where 3DPWM significantly outperforms prior methods due to higher-fidelity rollouts.
Table 1: Chamfer distance and reward correlation across embodiments and tasks (Best and second best methods are highlighted).
Table 7: Number of points for complete point cloud and action spaces of each of the tasks.

Figure 5: (Left) Adaptation to unseen tasks: We train 3DPWM dynamics on demonstrations generated on MugCleanup and Coffee tasks and show that it can be used to adapt to a much long-horizon task of CoffeePreparation and achieving 45% success rate. (Right) Sim2Real: We evaluate simto-real transfer of 3DPWM on PickApple, PickDrill, and PlaceApple. The static third-person camera setup and objects are shown in the top-right. While 3DPWM and ParticleFormer+perform similarly on the easier placing task, 3DPWM significantly outperforms on the picking tasks.

Figure 6: Point completion Data Generation: Given the mesh/point cloud of the object, we render depth maps from 100 random views around a sphere of 1 unit looking at (0, 0, 0), with the object in centered at the origin.

Figure 8: Lighting & Viewpoint condition: We tested the robustness of 3DPWM on PickApple task with two additional viewpoints as well as darker lighting condition. (Each plot is averaged over 20 trials.)

Figure 7: Point completion success & failures: We show few samples of the fine-tuned point cloud completion model. (Top) Successful point cloud completions on partial point clouds of apple and mustard bottle. (Bottom) Failure scenarios of the completion on Drill and Apple from the YCB dataset.
Table 6: Chamfer distance and reward correlation on both variants of ParticleFormer (+ and ∗) (Best and second best).

Figure 3: Qualitative rollout results of 3DPWM. Action-conditioned rollouts of 3DPWM over time for five tasks. Ground-truth trajectories are shown in purple, while predicted rollouts are shown in teal. The second column (with purple border) shows the initial observed point cloud, and all subsequent point clouds are generated by rolling out the model using actions from the ground-truth trajectory. A higher overlap between the purple and teal points indicate better accuracy of world model rollouts.
